pr_title: fix(platform-browser): key event handler should run in the correct zone
pr_body:
Close #38260 .

Currently the KeyEventPlugin handle key event such as `keydown.enter` and always run into `ngZone` no matter
which zone it is added. And this behavior is not consistent with the other event handlers.

So this commit fixes this issue.

Also it make sure the `event handler` in key event plugin call on the correct context object.

issue_context.title: KeyEventPlugin forces event handler in `ngZone`, the behavior is different with non key event handler.
comments: @JiaLiPassion why keydown listener should run outside of zone in your example?
@artaommahe, since the `keydown` listener is added outside of `ngZone`, you can check this issue for more information https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/37062

@JiaLiPassion hm, but new behavior looks counter-intuitive. Developer needs to know some angular core stuff to understand why click/keydown is running outside angular zone despite they are just declared in template like any other event listeners.

@artaommahe , I totally understand your concerns and agree with your point, but this issue and related PR doesn't introduce a `new` behavior. The current behavior (except the events like `keydown.enter`) is `outside` ngZone. ```
``` In this case, the current behavior is 1. the `button click` is outside of ngZone. 2. the `keydown` is inside ngZone. Which is not consistent. And most cases are like `button` click, so this issue and PR just make `keydown.enter` behaves the same way as `button click`. Of course we can discuss this behavior is correct/confuse or not in another issue.

Sure, I just add the `JSDoc` to explain this function.

@devversion , the reason not to use `this._zone.run()` directly is if we use `this.zone.run()` even we are already inside the `NgZone`, it will trigger another `ApplicationRef.tick()` and cause the `NG0101 nested ApplicationRef.tick()` error.
interesting, good thing to have this noted here 👍
